meta.scope: Chile batch 3 — Región Metropolitana / Santiago metro layer + copper & lithium mining depth + public-finance anchors. Tests capital-region density and the structural mining backbone.

candidates.title: Región Metropolitana de Santiago (RMS) — core statistical region
candidates.publisher: INE Chile + Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
candidates.description: Capital region and largest population concentration (~7.4–8.4 million depending on census vs survey frame). Primary domain for ENE, CASEN and many price/activity series. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average.
candidates.notes: Dominant metro node. CASEN 2024: income poverty 13.3% (vs national 17.3%); multidimensional poverty 19.7%. ENE regularly publishes RMS unemployment (recently ~9.6%). Censo 2024 population ~7.4 million in the region.

candidates.title: Gran Santiago / continuous urban agglomeration
candidates.description: Continuous urban fabric of the capital, spanning multiple communes of the Región Metropolitana. Functional metropolitan area for labour-market and price analysis.
referenced_by: Census geographic products and commune-level population
candidates.notes: Urban-agglomeration counterpart to the administrative Región Metropolitana. Commune-level census data (Puente Alto, Maipú, Santiago, La Florida, etc.) make the internal structure visible.

candidates.title: ENE — resultados Región Metropolitana de Santiago
candidates.description: Geographic cut of the National Employment Survey for the capital region, including provincial breakdowns inside the RMS.
candidates.notes: Practical vehicle for metro labour analysis. Recent moving quarter: RMS unemployment 9.6% (slightly above national). Provincial variation inside the region is reported (Cordillera, Talagante higher; others lower).

candidates.title: CASEN — resultados Región Metropolitana de Santiago
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
candidates.description: Regional cut of the CASEN survey providing income poverty, multidimensional poverty and living-conditions indicators for the capital region.
candidates.notes: Shows the capital region as lower-poverty than the national average under the updated methodology (13.3% income poverty vs 17.3% national in 2024).

candidates.title: Producción y exportaciones de cobre / Copper statistics
candidates.description: Official and industry statistics of mine copper production (Codelco + private), exports, and contribution to fiscal revenues. Chile remains the world’s largest copper producer (~24% of global output).
candidates.notes: Structural backbone of the Chilean economy and external accounts. 2024–2025 production in the 5.3–5.5 Mt range. Codelco ~24–29% of national output; private mining the rest. Copper is the dominant single export and a major fiscal contributor.

candidates.title: Codelco — producción y aporte fiscal
candidates.description: State copper producer. Statistical identity covering own production, total attributable production, EBITDA, and transfers to the Treasury.
candidates.notes: Largest single mining entity. 2025 own production ~1.33 Mt fine copper; consolidated contribution to the fisco reported in the USD 1.7–1.8 bn range. Also entering lithium via joint venture in the Salar de Atacama.

candidates.title: Producción de litio / carbonato de litio (Chile)
candidates.description: Physical and value statistics of lithium carbonate and related lithium production, concentrated in the Salar de Atacama. Rising component of non-metallic mining and of fiscal revenues (Corfo contracts).
candidates.notes: High-growth critical-mineral series. Visible in the IPMin (non-metallic mining) and in fiscal accounts (ingresos por litio de Corfo). Production in the hundreds of thousands of tonnes LCE; joint-venture developments continuing.

candidates.title: Comisión Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco) — statistical publications
candidates.description: Specialised public agency that compiles and disseminates copper and broader mining statistics, market analysis and production projections.
candidates.notes: Authoritative specialised source for copper production, costs, markets and fiscal contribution. Complements the broader INE industrial indices and Central Bank external accounts.

candidates.title: Estadísticas de finanzas públicas / Dirección de Presupuestos
candidates.publisher: Dirección de Presupuestos (DIPRES) — Ministerio de Hacienda
candidates.description: Official public-finance statistics covering central-government revenues (including copper and lithium), expenditure, and fiscal balance. Copper and lithium are explicitly tracked revenue lines.
candidates.notes: Public-finance counterpart to the mining production and trade statistics. Copper (Codelco + private mining taxation) and lithium (Corfo) are material and volatile components of fiscal revenue.

candidates.title: Censo 2024 — resultados Región Metropolitana
candidates.description: Regional and commune-level results of the 2024 Population and Housing Census for the capital region.
candidates.notes: Structural demographic baseline for the metro. Commune ranking (Puente Alto, Maipú, Santiago, La Florida, etc.) and ageing indices already published. Feeds survey frames and small-area estimation.

proposed_edges.basis: RMS results are the regional cut of the national employment survey.
RMS poverty and living-conditions figures are the regional cut of CASEN.
Copper production is the dominant component of the metallic-mining index.
Copper is the principal single export product in merchandise trade statistics.
Codelco is the largest single producer within national copper output.
Lithium appears inside the non-metallic mining component of the IPMin.
Copper-related revenues (Codelco transfers + private mining taxation) are explicit lines in the fiscal accounts.
Regional and commune results are geographic disaggregations of the national census.
